#6096. Hilton’s Cyber Week Bonus Is Worth Just $8—But You Can Stack Three Offers For 10,000 Points On A Single Night

Hilton Honors will give you 2,000 bonus points per stay if you book by Tuesday, December 1. I value Hilton points at 0.4 cents apiece. That’s $8 for a night at a Hampton Inn or $8 for a week at a Conrad. Book directly with Hilton. The booking window opened November 24, 2026, for stays completed November 25, 2026 through April 2, 2027. There’s no registration required or cap. (Hat tip to Head for Points.) For stays through December 31, 2026, register for More Points to Play before checkout. It adds 1,000 points at most hotels or 3,000 at listed luxury, lifestyle, resort and all-inclusive properties. With both offers that’s 3,000 points ($12) or 5,000 ($20). Award stays qualify for the fall offer. Hilton’s Cyber Week terms aren’t explicit on this but don’t exclude them. Book a Hilton Sale rate and pay the whole bill with a U.S. Hilton American Express card and you can earn another 5,000 points once per cardholder (book by December 22, stay by April 2). Book by December 1 and check out by December 31 to combine all three offers. That’s 8,000 bonus points ($32) at most hotels. At a property on the higher bonus list, one night can earn 10,000 bonus points ($40) before you count the usual hotel and card earnings. In the U.S. and Canada, the sale rate takes up to 20% off Hilton’s best available rate and requires booking at least seven days ahead. At most Hilton and Marriott brands, $100 in eligible room charges earns 1,000 base points. That’s $4 back at Hilton against about $6 at Marriott. Back in 2010, Hilton’s Jeff Diskin explained that Hilton got too little credit for what it gave every member and so promotions let them drive business. For years Hilton offered double points almost all the time. That lifted the return at most brands from 4% to 8% before elite or card bonuses. This year two months went by between the summer offer ending August 15 and the fall one starting October 15. Hilton seems to run promotions less frequently than they used to, but promotions are core to the program’s earning proposition being competitive. It’s worth repricing refundable Hilton stays booked before November 24. The fall offer already covers existing reservations, so it’s the Cyber Week add-on that’s worth considering (I wouldn’t bother rebooking if the room rate has gone up). #6094. Turkish Airlines Looks Up Rules For The Wrong Georgia — Passenger Loses A Week And $5,000

Turkish Airlines seems to have looked up the wrong Georgia when a passenger checked in, and came up with the wrong rules for travel. A Georgian journalist and his partner were flying from Washington Dulles via Istanbul to visit family in the country next door to Turkey. He says the airline turned them away over a “Swine and Bird Import Permit” for their two pet parakeets. That’s a permit you can get in Atlanta. The airline that holds the Guinness World Record for flying to the most countries flies to both Georgias. From Istanbul they’ll take you to Atlanta or to Tbilisi or Batumi. Turkish Airlines Boeing 777 approaching Washington Dulles in 2025, credit Acroterion The state of Georgia calls its form “Swine and Bird Travel Permit Registration.” The application asks for the destination state and ZIP code. Meanwhile, the Georgian consulate’s instructions for pet birds have identification and animal health requirements but not this kind of permit. Here’s their advice on taking pets to the country of Georgia. David Nikuradze shared his story with me about his August 14 flight. After more than 20 years covering Washington for Georgian television, he and his partner were moving to Portugal. They’d spent six months preparing, met with the manager of Turkish Airlines’ Washington office and made multiple visits to the vet. They showed up with six suitcases, two budgies and a health certificate endorsed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture. But Turkish told him to just leave the birds behind. That’s also what an 81-year-old woman says Frontier told her in Puerto Rico, after they’d flown her there with her parrot, Plucky. Washington Dulles, Credit David Benbennick Nikuradze says he brought stamped letters from the Georgian authorities back to the counter the next day confirming the birds didn’t need the permit. He still couldn’t get out for a week. Turkish told him earlier flights already had cats booked. Turksih allows parakeets in the cabin but not at the same time there’s also cats and on the same plane even in different cabins. They flew August 21 on their original veterinary paperwork. But first they had to pay Turkish to rebook, finnd a pet-friendly hotel in Manassas, rent a vehicle big enough for their luggage and buy a cage so the birds could get out of their carrier. Nikuradze puts the cost at more than $5,000. Two pet budgerigars on a cage, credit Anna Saccheri Turkish Airlines check-in staff seemed to think these passegners were flying Washington D.C. to Atlanta connecting through Istanbul, which is something only Eric Adams would do. Turkish has used dnata to check in passengers and verify their documents at Dulles. Outsourcing may have played a role here. I once wrote about Turkish Airlines sending a couple to Dhaka, Bangladesh, when they’d asked for Dakar, Senegal. When the flight attendant announced Dhaka, they figured that was how you said Dakar with a Turkish accent. The airline that holds the Guinness World Record for flying to the most countries flies to both Georgias. From Istanbul they’ll take you to Atlanta or to Tbilisi or Batumi.

Turkish Airlines Boeing 777 approaching Washington Dulles in 2025, credit Acroterion

The state of Georgia calls its form “Swine and Bird Travel Permit Registration.” The application asks for the destination state and ZIP code.

Meanwhile, the Georgian consulate’s instructions for pet birds have identification and animal health requirements but not this kind of permit. Here’s their advice on taking pets to the country of Georgia.

David Nikuradze shared his story with me about his August 14 flight. After more than 20 years covering Washington for Georgian television, he and his partner were moving to Portugal. They’d spent six months preparing, met with the manager of Turkish Airlines’ Washington office and made multiple visits to the vet. They showed up with six suitcases, two budgies and a health certificate endorsed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture. But Turkish told him to just leave the birds behind. That’s also what an 81-year-old woman says Frontier told her in Puerto Rico, after they’d flown her there with her parrot, Plucky.

Washington Dulles, Credit David Benbennick

Nikuradze says he brought stamped letters from the Georgian authorities back to the counter the next day confirming the birds didn’t need the permit. He still couldn’t get out for a week. Turkish told him earlier flights already had cats booked. Turksih allows parakeets in the cabin but not at the same time there’s also cats and on the same plane even in different cabins.

They flew August 21 on their original veterinary paperwork. But first they had to pay Turkish to rebook, finnd a pet-friendly hotel in Manassas, rent a vehicle big enough for their luggage and buy a cage so the birds could get out of their carrier. Nikuradze puts the cost at more than $5,000.

Two pet budgerigars on a cage, credit Anna Saccheri

Turkish Airlines check-in staff seemed to think these passegners were flying Washington D.C. to Atlanta connecting through Istanbul, which is something only Eric Adams would do.

Turkish has used dnata to check in passengers and verify their documents at Dulles. Outsourcing may have played a role here.

I once wrote about Turkish Airlines sending a couple to Dhaka, Bangladesh, when they’d asked for Dakar, Senegal. When the flight attendant announced Dhaka, they figured that was how you said Dakar with a Turkish accent. Turkish eventually admitted its booking agent had entered the wrong airport code and offered them two tickets anywhere it flew. For Nikuradze, I’d start by refunding the difference in airfare they paid.

#6092. American Airlines And Citi Test A $695 Business Card That Could Earn 50% More Miles And Loyalty Points

I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

American Airlines and Citi are working on a $695 AAdvantage Executive card for small businesses. It’s been an odd omission. The $695 United Club Business Card already earns 1.5 miles per dollar on everyday spending. Delta Air Lines has its $650 SkyMiles Reserve Business card. American’s Admirals Club card has been a consumer product.

Doctor of Credit shares some card designs that Citi is surveying. One looks a lot like the consumer Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] I’ve carried for a long time. However, the other would earn: 1.5 miles and 1.5 Loyalty Points per dollar on everyday purchases. Put $100,000 of bills on one employee’s card in a qualification year and the business would earn 150,000 redeemable miles. The employee would earn 150,000 Loyalty Points, enough for Platinum Pro, and the owner would earn 100,000 Loyalty Points, enough for Platinum. In January I wrote about Citi testing a $150 fee for the regular business card and the idea of replacing its $99 companion certificate with a flight discount. Citi went ahead with the fee and kept the certificate. So not everything being tested happens, and I’d put the strongest prediction on a card like this coming at a $695 annual fee with Admirals Club membership, realizing that the rest are potential options under consideration (and in some cases even controls that aren’t going to make the final product). Credit: Doctor of Credit What The Lounge Membership Gets A Business Both versions give the primary cardmember Admirals Club membership with up to two guests. The personal card also admits immediate family, which matters when there are four (or more) of you. Employee cards carry no additional annual fee. The company can buy lounge access for the people who travel, at $175 total for the first three and $175 apiece after that. So that’s basically the same as the consumer card, except that the annual fee plus lounge is optional rather. American charges $1,200 to $1,400 for full membership, depending on status. And the clubs are getting better. I prefer the newer American lounges to what United and Delta are building. My home club in Austin is slated to double in size and get an outdoor terrace. Someone who wants the lounge may already have gotten the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard®. But Citi’s going to want the smaller group of customers who want big company expenses on a business account. Some Ideas Being Surveyed For The Card Both versions shared from this survey would earn 4 miles per dollar on American Airlines and 12 on eligible hotel and car bookings through American. Both come with Group 4 boarding, priority check-in and screening, Omni Champion and Avis President’s Club status, up to $100 for inflight or club purchases, and $15 in Lyft credit after three eligible rides in a month. One largely copies the personal Executive card. It earns one mile and one Loyalty Point per dollar on ordinary spending, plus 10,000 Loyalty Points at each of four balances (50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000). The other awards 1.5 Loyalty Points on every eligible dollar the cardholder spends. It drops the four milestones, along with the two $250 American Airlines Vacations credits and two $100 inKind dining credits. Instead there’s $20 a month toward Melio or Xero and half off an annual Fox One and Wall Street Journal bundle (meh). It adds Sixt to the $120 Avis and Budget credit and covers a second domestic checked bag. But its two Omni free nights interest me. On the personal Executive card you enroll and complete a qualifying stay of at least two consecutive nights booked directly with Omni to earn one free night. If this didn’t require a stay to earn that would be exceptionally valuable (I’d probably redeem them in New York or worst case if I didn’t otherwise use them, down the street at Barton Creek Resort in Austin). I like the potential add-on of rewards for $100,000 in spending, since the consumer version doesn’t really give a strong incentive to actually spend money on the card (it’s a great one to get and keep, but spending is really only incentivized by the Loyalty Points). Here they’re surveying a choice of 2,500 Loyalty Points, two Flagship Lounge passes or a $200 flight discount. American sells the passes for $150 apiece, though I’d value them as an upgrade from the Admirals Club I can already visit. It’s probably best to just take the flight discount unless the points pushed someone over a status or reward threshold. The $200 adds just 0.2% across $100,000. But for someone already at $96,000 spend it’s worthwhile for the next $4,000. Would I Keep Two $695 American Airlines Cards? I have the regular Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees], and there’s a reason to spend on it even at one mile per dollar. Through December 31, 2028, eligible purchases on an employee’s card earn a Loyalty Point for the employee and another for the primary cardmember. Both survey designs call that a promotion. On the more interesting version of the premium business card, the extra half Loyalty Point goes to the person whose name is on the card. If employees pay the bills, the owner’s rate on those purchases stays at one. An owner who earns all four personal Executive bonuses from flying could give up 40,000 Loyalty Points by replacing the personal card with that one. The regular business card’s fee goes from $99 to $150 on January 24, 2027. At $100,000 of ordinary spending, E would cost $545 more and earn 50,000 more redeemable miles. That’s 1.09 cents per extra mile before valuing Omni nights or other benefits. If the alternative is a 2% cash back card with no annual fee, though, you’re giving up $2,000 and paying $695. You’d need nearly 1.8 cents apiece from the 150,000 miles to cover both with miles alone. Status remains the reason for spending on the card. A big initial bonus could make either version worth getting for a year. I’d keep my personal Executive and look at replacing my regular business card with this new one. So you play some primary/AU games. As I was just speculating on DoC, if I’m understanding the proposal correctly, you could get EP without flying by spending $133.33k. And you’d maximize by having the AU do the spending to get EP and then the primary would get PPro with 1x / 133k LP. That’s a significantly better spending for status proposition versus DL/UA. Plus stack with other AA cards (whether a personal Exec, Globe for flight streak, etc.), extra 1x LP on flying with the AA business program, and combine with actual flying… spend for status becomes even cheaper. Almost seems like too good of a deal.

I do think that eventually AA will raise status levels to match the LP accelerator levels with the personal Exec card – so gold will be 60k, plat 100k, ppro 175k and ep 250k. But we will see…

Honestly, Version L combined with the personal Executive Card and the legacy Globe card gets kinda silly at the lower end. Spend $55k and I think you end up with 110k LPs (15k from Globe, then you trip two batches of bonuses).

I’m afraid I’m unclear about whether the spend on employee cards would allow both the AU and the main cardholder to get LP’s as with the current business card.

Serious question. If I always fly business anyway, have a card that gives me lounge access, and purchase tickets using an AX Plat for 5X miles, is there any true inherent marginal value for something like AA Platinum or Platinum Pro (or any other airline high-tier loyalty level?

@Thing 1 – the marginal value in that case is twofold. First, platinum pro gets you oneworld emerald status. Depending on where you are flying, the ability to access first class lounges might be appealing. If you’re a LHR flier, the ability to use the BA First check-in area with private security that leads directly to the BA First lounge, for example – that’s something a business class ticket doesn’t buy you. Want to access Soho when flying out of JFK? Need to be OWE – a business class ticket just gets you Greenwich. You might value that, or may assign that no value.

The other thing that you might value are more miles as a result of being a higher status. So if you’re buying a $5,000 r/t cash business class ticket, you’d get 5x from Amex Plat and another 5x as a general AAdvantage member, but if you were PPro, you’d get 9x, or EP 11x. So that’s an additional 20-30k AA miles, which at 1.5cpm is another $300-450. Maybe that’s something you value, or maybe you’re already getting 50k miles between Amex/AA and getting another 20-30k miles would just be gravy that you don’t need on top of the turkey.

#6091. Pritzker accused of turning education tax credit into partisan fight by opting out of program: 'Sad to see'

Teach Coalition CEO Sydney Altfield argued that Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker’s decision to opt his state out of the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program — after several other Democratic governors opted into the program — will "put kids in the middle of partisan politics."

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, a Democrat, is being accused of putting partisan politics over kids' educational needs after he decided to opt out of the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program, prompting criticism from parents and education advocacy groups.

Pritzker announced on Tuesday that his state will not opt into the program, which was signed into law by President Donald Trump last year as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The governor described the program as a school voucher, while advocacy groups argued that he mischaracterized the plan.

"At a time when public school education needs investments more than ever, we should not siphon money from public schools for private education – especially as the Trump Administration's policies decimate education," Pritzker said in a statement. "We have a responsibility to do right by all of our students. Taxpayer funding should not subsidize donations to private schools that could discriminate based on religion, sexual orientation, or other characteristics."

The program allows people to receive federal tax credits for donations up to $1,700 to authorized scholarship-granting organizations (SGOs), which distribute the donated scholarship funds to eligible families to be used on private or public educational expenses, including private school tuition, tutoring services, textbooks and more.

GOV HOCHUL'S PLAN TO OPT NEW YORK INTO FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE PROGRAM DRAWS UNION OPPOSITION

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker opted his state out of the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program. (Eileen T. Meslar/Chicago Tribune)

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Teach Coalition CEO Sydney Altfield said her advocacy group is "extremely disappointed" in the governor for opting out of the program.

"Not only did he opt kids out of his state and families out of his state from receiving scholarships, but the program allows for Illinois residents to still claim the tax credit. And what that means is that money that should have and could have gone to students and families in Illinois will now just move over the border and flow out of state — over about $2 billion in estimated scholarship money that could have stayed in the state," she explained.

Pritzker said in his announcement that his opt-out reaffirms his commitment to strengthening the state’s public schools by ensuring federal taxpayer resources remain available to the students and communities they are intended to serve. ​

But Altfield took issue with Pritzker describing the program as a voucher, contending that it does not take money from public schools.

"In the same vein of him opting out, he completely misrepresented this program, saying that it is a voucher scheme. It is by definition not a voucher. It does not take a dollar from [the] public school systems. All it does is incentivize taxpayers to use their tax dollars, their federal tax dollars, not their state tax dollars, but federal tax dollars for scholarship money. And instead of it helping families in Illinois, it will now help families outside," Altfield said.

TRUMP EDUCATION OFFICIAL SAYS SCHOOL CHOICE PROGRAM WILL PUT PRESSURE ON DEM-LED STATES

The governor described the program as a school voucher, while advocacy groups argued that he mischaracterized the plan. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

"Public school students are able to take this money," she added. "And we know that the vast majority of Illinois students go to public schools. That means the vast majority of taxpayers in the state send their kids to public schools. So we will see the vast majority of taxpayers designating their tax dollars to help support SGOs that will, in turn, support public school kids and students."

Altfield also accused Pritzker of putting children in the crossfire of partisan politics over an issue that she believes has an opportunity for a rare showing of bipartisanship.

Three other Democrats — Colorado Gov. Jared Polis, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul and New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham — joined dozens of Republicans in opting their states into the program. However, some states that have already opted in will have a new Democratic governor in January, such as Colorado, where Gov.-elect Phil Weiser has already signaled plans to withdraw.

Kansas, Kentucky and North Carolina all have Democratic governors who did not want to join the program, but GOP legislatures in those states overrode the governors' vetoes.

"I think it's really sad to see — to put kids in the middle of partisan politics," Altfield said of Pritzker's opt-out. "Many blue state governors — Gov. Hochul, Gov. Polis in Colorado and the New Mexico governor — have put politics aside and have put kids first. And I think that if governors can peel back whatever misconceptions they are reading, and they can read the program for what it is, it is bipartisan. It will have bipartisan support because education, kids, families are the ones that are going to be successful in this."

Three Democrats — Colorado Gov. Jared Polis, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul and New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham — joined dozens of Republicans in opting their states into the program. (AP)

"I think we're going to see, and I hope we're going to see, more Democratic governors opting into this program before Jan. 1," she added.

Altfield also noted that the program could benefit families who may be struggling financially amid concerns in Illinois and across the nation about affordability.

"We all know that affordability is the number one issue that Democrats and everyone is running on and everyone is feeling a pinch of the penny across the country. And this is a real opportunity that has money flowing into the state of Illinois that could have helped families that are pinching every dollar. For the working mom of two or three or four, she may have one or two jobs, three jobs. Where is she sending her kid after school? Is she paying for after-school care? The tax credit program could have offered her a scholarship to help cover those costs," Altfield said.

"We talk about teachers paying out of pocket. It's been estimated that teachers pay well over $800 out of their pocket for school supplies. Imagine if every low-income kid came to school with all of the school supplies needed. That teacher would not have to pay out of pocket. It's small things like this that really add up in a pocketbook that are now not available to the families and the students in Illinois," she continued.

I’ve had first hand reports of this as well – the Trump administration has been refusing ESTAs to former U.S. citizens, requiring a full visa, even when they are citizens of and residing in visa waiver countries. The fact alone that they are ex-citizens keeps them from a smooth visit path, independent of any risk factors, and even if they’ve visited using ESTAs for 15 years.

This is a big deal for anyone thinking about renouncing US citizenship.

Many assume they can keep visiting the US after renunciation on ESTA based on their other citizenship. But there are more and more reports of former citizens being denied ESTA and told to apply for a visitor visa instead.

A visitor visa, unlike ESTA, generally requires a consular interview and proving that the applicant will leave after the visit. With family, businesses, or assets in the US, that could mean delays and refusals. This has to factor into the decision on whether or not to renounce.

#6088. Jeffries puts immigration bill high on Democratic priority list

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., holds a news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call)

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is signaling Democrats will move quickly on immigration legislation when the party reclaims the House in January, while acknowledging it still has work to do in shaping its healthcare agenda.

Jeffries, who is expected to secure his spot as the next speaker during a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday, identified immigration and health care as among the top priorities for the incoming majority during a Tuesday news conference.

“One of the things that we need to do is to move the Dream and Promise Act for DACA recipients and TPS recipients,” Jeffries said, referring to a Democratic bill introduced last year. “We should actually move that bill immediately.”

The proposal aims to create a path to citizenship for certain Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipients and Temporary Protected Status holders. Similar legislation has been a top priority for Democrats in both chambers for more than a decade, with Democrats unable to advance this bill in the House while Republicans have held the majority.

Jeffries also reiterated his calls to rein in Immigration and Customs Enforcement and redirect funding allocated to the agency through Republicans' budget law known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, while expressing a desire for bipartisan cooperation on immigration more broadly.

“We think the border should be safe and strong and secure, and we think our immigration system overall is broken,” Jeffries said. “We need to fix it in a comprehensive way, and certainly, it's our hope that a handful of Republicans will be willing to join us, so we can fix it in a bipartisan way.”

On healthcare, however, Jeffries offered fewer specifics, suggesting Democrats still have decisions to make before taking control of the chamber. Democrats broadly agree on the need to restore subsidies for plans purchased through health insurance markets that expired at the end of 2025. But the question of what additional steps the party should pursue with the goal of expanding coverage and lowering prices is likely to be a major test of Democratic leadership’s ability to find consensus among its robust new majority.

When asked how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that's all part of an ongoing conversation.”

The New York Democrat outlined several broader healthcare priorities, including reversing Medicaid cuts enacted under President Donald Trump, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits, all of which Democrats have vowed to do over the last year.

“Out of the gate, what we clearly have to do is fix our broken healthcare system in terms of the damage that's been done by Donald Trump and MAGA extremists over the last two years, and that clearly involves reversing the Medicaid cuts and extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits, and beginning to engage in supporting medical research, particularly things like research for pediatric cancer,” Jeffries added.

Democrats established a healthcare working group earlier this Congress, led by Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. and Terri Sewell, D-Ala., to gather perspectives and develop policy proposals as the party works toward a broader agenda.

Without an announced challenger, Jeffries has expressed confidence that he’ll secure the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who have said they remain “undecided” ahead of Wednesday’s elections. Jeffries, who was introduced as “Speaker Jeffries” on election night, said last week he was “very confident we’ll get there” and confirmed that the caucus will hold a recorded vote in the contest.

Rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to go forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives, many aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America, had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

Jeffries said Tuesday the approach mirrors the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who is best positioned to lead based on “track record, experience and vision.”

This report was corrected to reflect Rep. Nancy Pelosi’s status as a current member.

Southwest Airlines will give you a Companion Pass for a single holiday roundtrip, even if you book the cheapest Basic fare with points. From January 8 through March 3, 2027, you can bring someone on as many trips as you like for just the taxes and fees (from $5.60 each way). You can use points for your seat then, too.

Register for the Black Friday offer first, then book by 11:59 p.m. Central on Sunday, November 29. Put your Rapid Rewards number on the reservation when you book.

Already booked for Christmas? If the same award or paid ticket still costs the same, then register, cancel and rebook. And for a winter trip where you’ll use the pass, you can book your seat now and add your companion once the pass is active, as long as there’s still a seat for sale.

Southwest gets your Christmas booking this weekend and gives you the second seat after the holiday rush. If you earned the pass they offered in August, yours starts January 5 and also ends March 3. This offer adds zero days. You get one designated companion at a time across all your passes, with three changes for 2027 after you pick the first person.

I used to buy my ticket, bring my wife as my companion and redeem points for our daughter. With two kids, I’d register both parents. Each can earn a pass and designate a child. If one parent already earned August’s pass, only the other needs to qualify this time. Fly Austin to Orlando and back nonstop in February and the two kids’ tickets together would cost $22.40 in taxes and fees, even if both parents use points.

This year it takes 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points or 100 qualifying one-way flights to earn the full pass. Under the Rapid Rewards changes for 2027, unlimited companion travel comes with Platinum status starting January 1. That takes the same 100 flights – or 140,000 tier qualifying points. At 75 flights or 95,000 tier qualifying points you get three companion trips, each of which can be a roundtrip. What made the old pass so easy to earn was that a credit card initial bonus could cover most of those 135,000 points. Next year initial bonuses, referral and anniversary points, extra points from card bonus categories, and points from hotel and rental car partners stop counting toward the pass. A Southwest credit card earns one tier qualifying point per dollar, and cardmembers get a 10,000 point boost when they reach 130,000. Earning the full pass on card spend alone takes $130,000 in purchases. Southwest has also extended the credit card application deadline from December 2 to December 14. Apply by then and get approved, and the 80,000 or 90,000 point initial bonus can count toward the old 135,000 point requirement for a companion pass earned in 2026 even if you finish the required spending in early 2027. Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card (See rates and fees) earn 80,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card (See rates and fees) earn 90,000 bonus points after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. Any ordinary purchase points you need to close the gap still have to post in 2026. The pass you earn this way runs through December 31, 2027. #6085. Senators still see NDAA as chance for online safety legislation

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., delivers his opening statement during the hearing on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call)

Online safety advocates are looking to the annual defense policy bill for action on legislation to expand accountability for online platforms in cases of child sexual exploitation, as they also introduced legislation to make sure those cases aren’t forced into private arbitration.

Senators and advocates expressed support Tuesday for legislation that would expand the ability of victims of online sexual exploitation to sue social media platforms at a hearing focused on dangers children face on the gaming platform Roblox.

The Senate Judiciary Committee’s panel on Crime and Counterterrorism held the hearing after its Chairman Josh Hawley, R-Mo., and ranking member Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., introduced a bill Monday that would ban pre-dispute arbitration agreements from affecting cases where a minor was harmed online, including by sexual exploitation.

Hawley and Durbin also worked together on a separate bill to expand eligibility for victims of abuse to bring civil suits against online platforms that intentionally, knowingly or recklessly promoted or facilitated the abuse. It would also include penalties for certain platforms that fail to report child pornography violations on their sites.

That bill is included in a manager’s amendment to the Senate’s fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill. Durbin encouraged Congress to pass the NDAA “in the closing days” of the session because “protecting children is an important part of it.”

“I have a few weeks left in my service in the United States Senate,” said Durbin, who is retiring at the end of his term in January. “I’m thinking each day it’s coming to an end, but I want it to come [to an] end the right way.”

The subcommittee has spent much of the 119th Congress focused on harms to children online, including from artificial intelligence chatbots.

Tuesday’s hearing included testimony from survivors and experts on child exploitation on Roblox.

Hawley said that victims are bound by pre-dispute agreements with Roblox to settle claims through private arbitration, rather than in court.

“They slam the courthouse door shut in their faces,” Hawley said. “We’re talking about children now, child victims of sexual exploitation online are denied their day in court by the very company that has exposed them to the content to begin with.”

A spokesperson for Roblox said in a statement that “safety has been central” to the platform since its launch.

“We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat,” the spokesperson said. “A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company’s safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety.”

Myriam Gilles, a professor of law at Northwestern University, told the panel that a 2022 law that ended forced arbitration agreements for victims of sexual assault has gaps. She said Roblox has argued it does not apply to online actions, just “completed physical assault” and does not apply to platforms.

She also said that Hawley’s new arbitration bill would enhance the effects of his measure regarding civil suits by making sure those suits can be heard publicly if families so choose.

“Congress can pass laws, but if [suits] just get shunted into private arbitration, they’re doing no good in the world,” Gilles said. “A right to sue that ends in secret arbitration is a right in name only.”

The hearing came the same day that advocates, including reality TV personality and activist Paris Hilton, held a press conference to urge House action on a bill (S 1837) that would allow individuals to bring civil suits over nonconsensual intimate depictions generated by artificial intelligence or for possession or production of deepfake porn if there was also intent to disclose the images.

That bill passed the Senate in January but has not been taken up in the House.

Everyone knows Black Friday is a prime time to save on everyday purchases and holiday shopping. But did you know it’s also a great opportunity to book your next trip?

Travel operators, including many hotel brands and vacation rental platforms, tend to offer deep discounts on Black Friday (Nov. 27 this year), Cyber Monday (Nov. 30) and/or Travel Tuesday (Dec. 1). So, now is the time to start thinking about where you want to go this holiday season — or even into 2027, as many of these deals have generous booking windows.

Here, we’ve rounded up the best hotel and lodging deals of 2026 so you can get a head start on savings.

Related: TPG's guide to Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals

Hilton's latest sale is not limited to Cyber Week. From now through Dec. 22, 2026, Hilton Honors members can book participating hotels in the U.S. and Canada for 20% off. You have until ‌April‌ 2, 2027, to complete travel.

Plus, if you register for the More Points to Play offer, you can score up to 3,000 bonus points on every stay through the end of the year.

With this Black Friday and Cyber Monday deal, World of Hyatt members can save up to 25% on qualifying stays at participating hotels and resorts worldwide and enjoy complimentary breakfast at participating hotels in Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

Nonmembers can save up to 20%, but since membership is free, you may as well join the program to maximize your savings.

Book by Dec. 8, 2026, for stays through April 30, 2027.

This is another sale where it pays to be a loyalty member. With IHG's Black Friday promo, One Rewards members can save up to 30% at participating hotels worldwide while non-members can save up to 20%. Book by Dec. 3, 2026, for stays between Nov. 21, 2026 and April 30, 2027.

Plus, IHG is offering up to 60% off at select Iberostar Beachfront Resorts — and for those who like to plan ahead, the travel window is generous. Book by Dec. 1, 2026, for stays through Oct. 31, 2028 (stay dates vary by location).

This Cyber Week, Marriott Bonvoy is unwrapping deep discounts at thousands of participating hotels and resorts worldwide.

To get the maximum savings of 25%, all you have to do is be a Bonvoy member and book through the program's mobile app. Meanwhile, members and nonmembers who book on Marriott's website will save 15%.

Book from Nov. 24 to Dec. 1 for stays between Nov. 29, 2026, and May 2, 2027.

In addition, Marriott Bonvoy is offering two seasonal bonuses. To celebrate Giving Tuesday, the program will match five times the points donated to various charitable causes through its LoveTravels platform between Dec. 1-8. And you can save 30% site-wide at Marriott Bonvoy Boutiques from Nov. 17 through Dec. 2, with free shipping from Nov.30 onward.

Accor is offering savings of up to 35% on hotel stays across the Americas, and ALL Accor members can save an additional 10%. Plus, you can earn up to 4 reward points per dollar spent in the ALL Accor app.

Book between Nov. 23 and Dec. 2, 2026, for travel from Dec.18, 2026, to Dec. 19, 2027.

Preferred Hotels & Resorts, the world’s largest independent hotel brand, is offering 35% off stays of two nights or more at participating hotels worldwide. This applies to the sustainability-minded Beyond Green collection as well.

Book between Nov. 23 and Dec. 3, 2026, for travel through June 30, 2027.

Ready for a beach getaway? With Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, you can score 30% to 65% off at more than 300 hotels across Latin America and the Caribbean. Plus, Wyndham Rewards members can save an extra 12% on promotional rates.

Book between Nov. 19 and Dec. 4 for stays between Nov. 19, 2026, and Oct. 31, 2027.

Rove Miles has multiple hotel deals this Black Friday, including 10 Rove Miles per dollar spent on new Loyalty Eligible hotel bookings — on top of the hotel points and elite night credits you'll earn through the property's loyalty program.

Rove is also offering a transfer bonus to ALL Accor from Thanksgiving Day to Cyber Monday. The bonus miles you can earn depend on what Rove elite status you hold:

That's not all. Rove's other travel deals include airline transfer bonuses, bonus miles on gift cards and more.

If you're not yet a member, you can score 1,500 bonus miles when you join Rove through TPG's link and an additional 5,000 bonus miles on your first hotel booking over $500 with code "BRIANKELLY500."

Priceline's vast menu of Black Friday travel deals — on flights, car rentals, vacation packages, cruises and more — includes hotels as well. Travelers can score up to 40% at select hotels, with the most savings on stays of two nights or more. Plus, you can save $100 on select Disney destination hotels with code "DISNEYBF100."

Members of Priceline's VIP loyalty program (it's free to join) get access to the above deals starting Nov. 16, and the sale opens to nonmembers on Nov. 23. It will run through Dec. 2 at 9 a.m. Eastern.

Priceline will also be dropping limited-time flash sales for Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Travel Tuesday:

As with Priceline, the One Key loyalty family — Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo — has a slew of travel deals coming up for Black Friday, Cyber Monday and Travel Tuesday. Among them, you’ll find rates slashed up to 50% at thousands of hotels and vacation rentals.

Even better, these deals are valid for travel through Dec. 30, 2027, giving you plenty of time to plan.

Hotels.com has also teased a special coupon for an extra 15% off, set to drop on Cyber Monday.

If you'd like to give the gift of travel, consider buying a Hotels.com gift card this holiday season. You can save 10% on gift cards of $100-plus and 15% on $300-plus from Nov. 23 through Dec. 31.

Is a vacation rental more your style? At Vrbo, travelers can save hundreds of dollars when booking a vacation rental 60 days in advance. Use the Early Booking and Weekly Stay discount filters to search for deals.
